questions.question_text: A population has P(D)=0.02, P(+|D)=0.90, P(+|not-D)=0.10. D and not-D partition the population. (a) Find P(+). (b) Find P(D|+). (c) Explain why sensitivity 0.90 is not the answer to (b).
questions.reference_solution: (a) 0.90*0.02+0.10*0.98=0.116. (b) 0.018/0.116=9/58, about 0.1551724. (c) Sensitivity conditions on D, whereas the posterior conditions on +; the base rate and false positives affect the posterior.

a.criterion: Includes both partition terms and obtains 0.116.

c.criterion: Distinguishes conditioning direction and accounts for base rate/false positives.

questions.question_text: Two independent fair coins have Omega={HH,HT,TH,TT}, each mass 1/4. Let A={HH,HT}, B={HH,TH}, N=empty set. (a) Find P(A|B). (b) Is P(A|N)=0? Explain.
questions.reference_solution: (a) (1/4)/(1/2)=1/2. (b) No. P(N)=0 makes the elementary conditional undefined. The zero numerator does not authorize division by zero.

questions.question_text: One fair die is rolled. Let A={1}, B={2}. Are A and B independent? Show the calculation and distinguish independence from disjointness.
questions.reference_solution: They are disjoint, but not independent: P(A intersection B)=0 while P(A)P(B)=(1/6)(1/6)=1/36. The product criterion fails.

a.criterion: One point each for disjointness, intersection zero, product 1/36, and dependent conclusion.

questions.question_text: For any event A and null event N with P(N)=0, prove A and N independent by the product definition. Does this make elementary P(A|N) defined?
questions.reference_solution: Since A intersection N is a subset of N, its probability is zero. This equals P(A)P(N), so independence holds. Elementary P(A|N) remains undefined because the denominator is zero; independence does not remove that condition.

a.criterion: Subset monotonicity plus product equality, valid for any null N.

b.criterion: Retains P(N)>0 requirement for elementary conditioning.
